newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cattle, hog plants closed Independence Day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cattle, hog plants closed Independence Day.

text.p: Major U.S. cattle and hog slaughter plants will be closed Friday in obervance of the Independence Day holiday, company officials said.

IBP Inc, Excel Corp, a unit of Cargill Inc, Smithfield Foods and its subsidiary John Morrell and Co, Hormel Foods Corp, Thorn Apple Valley Inc, ConAgra Inc subsidiaries Swift and Co (pork) and Monfort (beef) and Farmland Industries officials all said their respective cattle and hog slaughter and processing plants would be closed.
There could be light operations by smaller processing facilities or specialty plants, several sources said.
There were 4,000 cattle and 39,000 hogs slaughtered last year on Independence Day, which fell on a Thursday, USDA statistics showed.
Saturday hog slaughter was seen light, with only a handful of plants open because of ongoing unprofitable operating margins, plant officials and market sources said.
Hog slaughter on Saturday was seen at 10,000-12,000 head, compared with 37,000 last Saturday, said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst with Alaron Trading Corp.
Monday hog slaughter also was seen light and could range 280,000-282,000 head, compared with 302,000 estimated by USDA the previous week, Levitt said.
Cattle slaughter on Saturday was seen average to slightly higher at 65,000-95,000 head, compared with 69,000 the previous week and Monday was seen average in the low 130,000-head range, Levitt said.
